title: What Is Influencer Marketing? How It Works, Types, and Examples
summary: Learn what influencer marketing is, how it works, the types of influencers, real campaign examples, and how to build a strategy that drives measurable results.
body_markdown:
## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is influencer advertising?


Influencer advertising is a paid partnership in which a brand compensates a creator to share branded content with their audience, typically through sponsored posts, videos, reviews, or affiliate recommendations. Compensation can include a fee, free products, or commission, and campaigns work best when the creator and platform fit the business goal.


### What is the 3-3-3 rule in marketing?


The 3-3-3 rule is a content and attention framework suggesting you have roughly three seconds to capture attention, three seconds to establish relevance, and three seconds to deliver your core message. In influencer marketing, this reinforces why short-form video and strong creator-led openings drive better results.


### How many followers do you need to be a paid influencer?


You do not need a minimum follower count to become a paid influencer; nano and micro creators with even a few thousand focused followers regularly earn compensation. Brands pay for audience fit and engagement, not size alone, so smaller communities with genuine interest can be highly valuable.


### How much does influencer marketing make?


Influencer marketing generates billions in spend annually and continues to grow as social commerce expands. For individual creators, earnings vary widely by audience size, niche, and format, ranging from free products for nano creators to substantial fees, commissions, and live shopping revenue for larger accounts.


### How many followers do you need to make $100,000?


Many creators reach six figures with highly engaged audiences of tens of thousands by combining sponsorships with social commerce sales.


### How is influencer marketing different from celebrity endorsement?


Influencer marketing relies on a creator speaking directly to their own audience, often in a specific niche, while celebrity endorsement depends on broad public recognition. A celebrity can also be an influencer, but the terms describe different strengths: fame versus creator-led storytelling and audience relevance.


### Why does influencer marketing work for brands?


Influencer marketing works because creator recommendations appear in a familiar, trusted content environment where followers actively watch, comment, and ask questions. When the creator has a genuine connection to the product category, a demonstration feels more relevant and credible than a conventional ad, driving measurable awareness and sales.
